title: I Took the Disc-Golf Tee-Time Sheet to the Marshal Who Cut the Pad

parts.text: I signed hole 1 at 9:03 a.m. and the marshal's cart was already on the pad without a name. The kiosk sheet said: SIGN THE TEE. MARSHALS YIELD TO CARDS. I was thirty-eight, Saturday card, holding a signed line. Marshal Vic threw a driver. "Marshals are the course." I photographed the empty sign-in, the cart, and his throw. Then I logged a pad cut. At 9:11 parks asked why Vic's cart was on a unsigned tee. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Parks can see Vic's cart on hole 1 without a signed tee line.

social.video_title: The marshal threw from an unsigned pad — Part 1/2
social.description: Disc golf, a kiosk sheet, and a cart on the tee. I logged the cut. Would you have waited for a name?

parts.text: Vic called it a safety check until parks asked for the log. I printed the cut, the photo, and the sheet. He signed like a card. Vic yielded and told the next group safety was always about optics. Optics is a word marshals use when a cart exists. Tee policy now has a second line: MARSHALS SIGN. I keep my line. Vic queues. The pad finally looks like a tee, not a shortcut. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.

social.description: Pad-cut log, a signed marshal, and a second line. Was safety ever an empty kiosk?
